english: Let $L$ be the locus of the complex numbers $z$ satisfying $|z|=|z-2-i|$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, and let $R$ be the ray $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. The image of $R$ in the line $L$ is a ray which meets the real axis at the point $(x_{0},0)$. Then the value of $x_{0}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $L$ उन सम्मिश्र संख्याओं $z$ का बिन्दुपथ है जो $|z|=|z-2-i|$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है, तथा $R$ किरण $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ है। रेखा $L$ में $R$ का प्रतिबिम्ब एक किरण है जो वास्तविक अक्ष को बिन्दु $(x_{0},0)$ पर मिलती है। तब $x_{0}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $L$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment from $0$ to $2+i$: $4x+2y=5$; so the image of the vertex $O$ of $R$ in $L$ is $B=2+i$
$R$: $y=x$, $x>0$, meets $L$ at $6x=5$: $P=\left(\dfrac{5}{6},\dfrac{5}{6}\right)$; $P$ lies on $L$, so it is its own image
Image ray: from $B(2,1)$ through $P$, direction $\left(-\dfrac{7}{6},-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)\parallel(-7,-1)$; points $(2-7s,\,1-s)$, $s>0$
solution_full: $|z|=|z-(2+i)|$ is the set of points equidistant from $0$ and $2+i$, the perpendicular bisector of that segment. With $z=x+iy$: $x^{2}+y^{2}=(x-2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}$, i.e. $4x+2y=5$.

The image of a point $A$ in the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is $B$. So the image of the vertex $O$ of the ray $R$ (the vertex itself is not on $R$, but the image ray starts there) is $B=2+i$. Check with the image formula: the foot of $O$ on $4x+2y=5$ is $\dfrac{5}{20}(4,2)=(1,0.5)$, and the image is twice the foot, $(2,1)$.
$R$ is $\{(t,t):t>0\}$. It meets $L$ where $6t=5$: $P=\left(\dfrac{5}{6},\dfrac{5}{6}\right)$, with $t>0$, so the ray does meet $L$. A point of $L$ is its own image.
Reflection maps the ray from $O$ through $P$ onto the ray from $B$ through $P$. Its direction is $P-B=\left(-\dfrac{7}{6},-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)$, parallel to $(-7,-1)$.
Points of the image ray: $(2-7s,\,1-s)$ for $s>0$. It meets the real axis when $1-s=0$, $s=1>0$, at $x_{0}=2-7=-5$.
(Direction check by reflecting the unit vector $(1,1)/\sqrt{2}$ of $R$ in $L$, normal $(2,1)$: $(1,1)-\dfrac{2\cdot3}{5}(2,1)=\left(-\dfrac{7}{5},-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)$, the same direction.)
originality_note: New: the perpendicular-bisector locus is used as a mirror whose defining points give the image of the ray's vertex at once, and the ray's meeting point with the mirror fixes the image direction (way 5). Closest known: image of a point in a line; locus |z - a| = |z - b|. Different because: a ray, not a point, is reflected, and the shortcut (image of 0 is 2+i) comes from the locus itself.

concept_use.Perpendicular bisector, ray and angle lo: |z| = |z-2-i| is the perpendicular bisector 4x+2y = 5; arg z = pi/4 is the ray y = x, x > 0, which meets it at (5/6, 5/6).
concept_use.Foot of perpendicular and image of a poi: The image of O in L is 2+i (twice the foot (1, 0.5)); points of L are fixed, so the image ray runs from 2+i through (5/6, 5/6).

key_step: Image of O in the bisector of O and 2+i is 2+i; the image ray passes through the point where R meets L.
justification: Routine chain of three steps (bisector equation, image of a point, line through two points) with one convenient observation. Level 2, like 2026-P2-Q1 (L2) in length.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, locus and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that R meets L (at t = 5/6 > 0), so the image ray passes through that point, and that the image ray (s > 0) reaches the real axis. Answer -5, negative integer. No change.
